xian-ranhou-zai.intro_tr: The 先...然后...再... structure is used to describe the ORDER in which a series of actions occur and corresponds to the Turkish pattern "first... then... later...". 先[xiān] means "first/firstly", 然后[ránhòu] means "after that/then", and 再[zài] here does not mean "again" but rather "the next step in sequence". These three words do not have to be used together in a single sentence; they can be combined as 先...然后..., 先...再..., or 先...然后...再... in two or three parts. Each verb phrase comes after its own subject and before the verb; this structure is very frequently used in both spoken and written language and is one of the basic conjunctions of HSK3 level. The most important point for zero-level students is: 先 and 再 come immediately before the verb, while 然后 stands at the beginning of the sentence as a "bridge" word connecting two clauses.

tables.caption_tr: Components and Functions of the Structure
rows: "ondan sonra, sonra" — bir sonraki eylemi önceki ile bağlar
"sırada sonra, daha sonra" — genelde sondaki eylemi işaretler ("tekrar" anlamında DEĞİL)
"en sonunda" — isteğe bağlı, listeyi kapatan güçlü vurgu
footnotes_tr: 再 here should not be confused with 再 meaning 'again/repeatedly' (e.g., 再见); in the context of sequential actions it only carries the meaning 'the next step'.

tables.caption_tr: Possible Combinations and Pattern Sentences

xiang-resemble.intro_tr: 像 [xiàng] is a very common verb in Chinese meaning 'to resemble, to be like' and is used to create similarity between two things or people. The most basic usage is simply the structure A + 像 + B (A resembles B); to express similarity in a more emphatic and vivid way, the pattern A + 像 + B + 一样 [yíyàng: "same, like"] (+ adjective/verb) is often used together. 像 can be used both as a predicate on its own (她像妈妈) and within an adverbial structure modifying a verb (跑得像风一样快). Its negation is 不像; for questions, the pattern 像不像 is used or 吗 is added to the end of the sentence. Additionally, 像 at the beginning of a list frequently appears with the meaning 'for example, for instance'.

tables.caption_tr: 像 (xiàng) Basic Sentence Patterns
rows: 她像她妈妈。[Tā xiàng tā māma.]
他像哥哥一样高。[Tā xiàng gēge yíyàng gāo.]
A + 像 + B + 一样 + Sıfat/Fiil
她的脸像苹果一样红。[Tā de liǎn xiàng píngguǒ yíyàng hóng.]
A + V + 得 + 像 + B + 一样
他跑得像风一样快。[Tā pǎo de xiàng fēng yíyàng kuài.]
像 + B + 这样/那样 + (的) + İsim
像他这样的人不多。[Xiàng tā zhèyàng de rén bù duō.]
footnotes_tr: Adding 一样 makes the similarity more emphatic and vivid; the sentence is also correct without 一样 but is simpler.

tables.caption_tr: Negative and Question Forms with 像
rows: 他不像他爸爸。[Tā bú xiàng tā bàba.]
不像 + B + 那么/这么 + Sıfat
今天不像昨天那么冷。[Jīntiān bú xiàng zuótiān nàme lěng.]
Bugün dün kadar soğuk değil (derece karşılaştırması).
我像老师吗?[Wǒ xiàng lǎoshī ma?]
这个像不像真的?[Zhège xiàng bu xiàng zhēn de?]
Bu gerçeğe benziyor mu? (V-不-V soru formu)
他一点儿都不像他哥哥。[Tā yìdiǎnr dōu bú xiàng tā gēge.]

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of 像 with Other Similarity Structures

frequency-complement.intro_tr: Frequency complement (次, 遍, 趟) is a group of "number + measure word" used after a verb to indicate how many times an action is performed; it corresponds to expressions like "twice, three times" in Turkish. 次[cì] is the most general and neutral measure word and counts the number of repetitions of any action. 遍[biàn], on the other hand, emphasizes that an action is performed COMPLETELY, thoroughly, once or several times from beginning to end (used with verbs that have a "process" such as reading, watching, listening, telling). 趟[tàng] is especially used with motion verbs that involve going and coming (去, 来, 跑) and carries the meaning of a "trip, tour". The position of the frequency complement in the sentence changes depending on the type of object (noun or pronoun); therefore, word order rules must be learned carefully.

zhiyou-cai.intro_tr: The 只有[zhǐyǒu]...才[cái]... pattern corresponds to the Turkish "only if..., then..." structure and specifies a NECESSARY/INDISPENSABLE single condition for a result to occur. The 只有 part indicates the condition, while the 才 part expresses the result that will never occur unless this condition is met; that is, it carries the meaning "there is no other way, only if it happens this way." This structure differs from the 只要[zhǐyào]...就[jiù]... pattern which indicates a sufficient condition: while 只要...就... says "this is sufficient, other ways are also possible," 只有...才... says "this is indispensable, this is the only way out." In a sentence, 只有 generally appears at the beginning of the conditional clause, while 才 appears right after the subject of the result clause and before the verb. It is a fundamental conjunction pattern frequently encountered at the HSK3 level and commonly used in both formal and colloquial speech.

ba-construction-basic.title_tr: 把 (bǎ) Structure Basis — Bringing the Object Forward
ba-construction-basic.intro_tr: The 把 (bǎ) structure is a special sentence pattern in Chinese that changes the normal Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) order by placing the object before the verb, after 把. The purpose is to emphasize the RESULT of an action performed on an object or what STATE the object is brought into; therefore, a "把 sentence" usually carries the meaning "what did I do with something / where did I put it / how did I transform it". The basic rule is: the object that comes after 把 must be something KNOWN TO BOTH THE SPEAKER AND LISTENER, something definite (that is, not "a book" but "that book/this book"). Furthermore, the verb can never stand alone; after the verb, there must always be added a "tail" such as 了, a complement (result, direction, place) or a reduplication. This page shows the most basic skeleton of the structure; for advanced constraint rules, see the topic "把 Structure Full Scope".

you-you.intro_tr: The 又...又... (yòu...yòu...) structure is used to express two characteristics, states, or actions that are simultaneously valid for the same subject, and it corresponds to the Turkish pattern "both... and..." (hem... hem de...). Usually two adjectives (又+A+又+B) or two verbs (又+V1+又+V2) are used in sequence, emphasizing that both are simultaneously correct/valid. This 又 should not be confused with the 又 meaning "again/repeat" — this is a separate, idiomatic usage. The two combined elements should generally be in the same emotional tone (both positive or both negative) and should not contradict each other; for example, "又高又矮" (both tall and short) would be illogical. It is a basic and practical pattern at HSK3 level, frequently used in spoken language.

gen-yiyang.intro_tr: The structure 跟...一样 [gēn...yíyàng] is used to compare two things and express that there is no difference between them, meaning 'A is the same as B.' 跟 [gēn] here is a preposition meaning 'with,' and 一样 [yíyàng] is an adjective meaning 'same, in the same way.' The structure is generally formed as A + 跟 + B + 一样 (+ adjective/verb), and 和 [hé] can also be used instead of 跟 in spoken language. The negative form is 不一样 [bù yíyàng] meaning 'not the same.' This pattern is a basic comparison structure frequently encountered at HSK3 level, and unlike the comparison structure with 比 [bǐ], it expresses equality/similarity rather than superiority.

topic-comment.intro_tr: In Chinese, sentences do not always follow a strict Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) order; a very common pattern is also "first the topic (话题), then a comment about this topic (说明)" structure. An element that is known, definite, or intended to be emphasized (usually an object, but can also be time, place, or even an entire clause) is moved to the beginning of the sentence, and then the remaining part continues with the normal Subject+Verb structure. In the example "那本书我看过", "那本书" (that book) is the topic, and "我看过" (I read) is a comment about this topic — the object is moved before the verb, to the very beginning of the sentence. This structure is similar to emphatic inverted sentences in Turkish like "That book, I read it" and is used very frequently in both spoken and written language. The difference from the 把 structure is that the 把 character is not used and there is generally no requirement for a resultative complement.

我把那本书看完了。[Wǒ bǎ nà běn shū kànwán le.]
把 kelimesi zorunludur; nesneye yapılan işlemin SONUCU vurgulanır, genelde tümleç gerekir.

geng-comparative.title_tr: 更 (gèng): "Even more" — Degree Adverb That Reinforces Comparison
geng-comparative.intro_tr: 更[gèng] is a degree adverb in Chinese meaning "more, even more" and always comes BEFORE an adjective or some emotion/state verbs. The most common usage is together with the comparison structure 比[bǐ]: the pattern "A 比 B 更 + adjective" means "A is even more [adjective] than B"; the 更 here reinforces an already existing superiority. 更 can also be used alone (without 比) meaning "even more compared to the previous situation." The point that confuses students most is the difference between 更 (even more / comparison reinforcer), 最 (most, superlative degree) and 还 (still, moreover — sometimes close to 更 but softer). 更 never comes directly before nouns; for noun comparisons other structures (like 比较) are needed.

ruguo-jiu.intro_tr: The 如果[rúguǒ]...就[jiù]... structure is the most basic and most frequently used equivalent in Chinese of the Turkish "if... then..." pattern. 如果[rúguǒ] initiates the conditional clause, while 就[jiù] connects the result that will occur when this condition is met. This structure can be used comfortably in both everyday speech and written language, which is why it is one of the most important conjunctions that need to be learned at HSK3 level. The most critical rule to remember: 就[jiù] always comes AFTER the subject and BEFORE the verb — it never comes at the beginning of a sentence. In the tables below, you can find the structure of the pattern, its frequently used variations, and its differences from similar conditional conjunctions.

jiu-vs-cai.title_tr: 就 (jiù) vs 才 (cái): Early/Late Emphasis
jiu-vs-cai.intro_tr: 就 [jiù] and 才 [cái] are two important adverbs that come before the verb and indicate whether an event happens "early or late", "quickly or slowly". 就 [jiù] typically describes a situation that happens BEFORE expected, QUICKLY and EASILY, and usually has 了 [le] added at the end of the sentence. 才 [cái], on the other hand, emphasizes a situation that happens AFTER expected, LATE or DIFFICULT, and in this structure, 了 [le] is generally not added at the end of the sentence. When used with numbers, 就 [jiù] means "just this much is enough/sufficed" (scarcity, surprise), while 才 [cái] means "only this much happened/sufficed" (abundance, impatience). This pair appears especially in conditional patterns like 只要...就... and 只有...才....

yidianr-youdianr.title_tr: 一点儿[yìdiǎnr] vs 有点儿[yǒudiǎnr]: Difference of 'a little'
yidianr-youdianr.intro_tr: Although both 一点儿[yìdiǎnr] and 有点儿[yǒudiǎnr] are translated as "a little" into English, their positions in sentences, meanings, and emotional tones are completely different. 一点儿[yìdiǎnr] comes AFTER an adjective/verb and usually expresses a comparison or a request (neutral/positive tone); 有点儿[yǒudiǎnr], on the other hand, comes BEFORE an adjective/verb and mostly indicates an unwanted, negative situation. Confusing these two is one of the most common mistakes made by everyone learning Chinese. With the tables below, you will learn their positions, meanings, and typical mistakes step by step.

zhiyao-jiu.title_tr: 只要...就... (If only... Then...) — Sufficient Condition Conjunction
zhiyao-jiu.intro_tr: The 只要[zhǐyào]...就[jiù]... pattern is a very common conjunction structure that means "if only ... then ..." and expresses SUFFICIENT CONDITION (sufficient condition). 只要 comes at the beginning of the condition clause, while 就 comes at the beginning of the result clause (after the subject), emphasizing that the realization of this condition guarantees the result without needing any other condition. When the same subject is used in both clauses, the subject is usually stated before 只要; in cases of different subjects, each clause has its own subject and the second subject appears before 就. This structure is frequently confused with 只有[zhǐyǒu]...才[cái]... (mandatory/only condition) structure, which has a stricter and "only way" meaning; the difference between them is shown in the comparison table below. For negative conditions, it can be used as 只要不... or 只要没(有)...

Aynı özne her iki fiil için de geçerlidir; özne bir kez, 只要'dan önce söylenir.

directional-complements-compound.title_tr: Compound Directional Complements (起来, 下去, 出来...)
directional-complements-compound.intro_tr: Compound directional complements are formed by the combination of a simple directional verb (上[shàng], 下[xià], 进[jìn], 出[chū], 回[huí], 过[guò], 起[qǐ]) with the word 来[lái] or 去[qù], and when added after a verb, they describe the direction of movement in detail. For example, 起来[qǐlai] = 起[qǐ] (rising direction) + 来[lái] (toward the speaker). 来[lái] indicates movement toward the speaker/listener, while 去[qù] indicates movement away from the speaker. These structures carry both concrete movement (up, down, in, out, back, across) and very frequently encountered metaphorical/abstract meanings (the beginning of an action, its continuation, emergence, becoming fixed). At HSK3 level, both the grammatical rules and metaphorical uses of these complements must be learned separately because they are extremely common in everyday speech.

tables.caption_tr: Simple Directional Verb + 来/去: Complete Table of Compound Directional Complements

de-adverbial.intro_tr: 地[de] is a structural particle that converts an adjective or adjective phrase into an ADVERB and places it IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the verb; it describes "how it is done". Basic pattern: Adjective/Adverb Phrase + 地[de] + Verb, for example 慢慢地走[mànmàn de zǒu] "to walk slowly". In single-syllable plain adjectives (like 快走) 地 is generally not used, but in two-syllable adjectives and especially in reduplicated (AABB or AA) adjectives 地 is almost mandatory. 地[de] in pronunciation is exactly the same as 的[de] and 得[de], so you need to distinguish the three based on their positions: 的 comes before a noun, 得 comes after a verb/adjective, and 地 comes before a verb. This page summarizes 地's basic usage rules, common adverbial patterns, and typical mistakes in tables.

a-particle.intro_tr: 啊 (a) is a particle added to the end of sentences that emphasizes the speaker's emotions (surprise, admiration, impatience, joy, etc.) or makes a question, request, or command more intimate and gentle. Semantically, it has no concrete equivalent; its function is purely about intonation and emotional expression. The pronunciation (and sometimes the writing) can change to 呀[ya], 哇[wa], or 哪[na] depending on the final sound of the preceding syllable — this is called 'sound harmony' (音变[yīnbiàn]). At HSK3 level, it is an indispensable particle for natural and fluent Chinese, frequently encountered in both everyday conversation and written dialogues.

footnotes_tr: In written language, using 啊 all the time is also acceptable; 呀/哇/哪 is preferred more in everyday conversation and literary texts.
In formal correspondence, the plain 啊 form is generally used; sound-harmonized variants are specific to spoken language.

rang-jiao-causative.title_tr: 让 / 叫 (ràng/jiào): Causative 'To Make/Cause' Structure
rang-jiao-causative.intro_tr: 让[ràng] and 叫[jiào] are causative verbs that correspond to the Turkish meanings of "to make do, to cause, to allow". The structure is as follows: Subject + 让/叫 + Person (being made to do) + Verb (Clause). That is, when saying "my mother made me do it", first comes the person causing it, then 让/叫, then the person receiving the command, and finally the action being performed — unlike in Turkish where a suffix is added to the verb, a separate word is used. 让[ràng] can mean both "to make do/to tell" and "to allow" and is softer/broader in usage; 叫[jiào] generally carries a meaning of verbal command/instruction and feels slightly more imperious in spoken language. For negation 不[bù] or 别[bié] come right before 让/叫: 不让/别让 (not to allow/not allowing), 不叫/别叫 (not to command/not commanding).

shi-de-construction.title_tr: 是...的 [shì...de] Structure: Time/Place/Method Emphasis in Past Actions
shi-de-construction.intro_tr: The 是...的 [shì...de] structure is used to emphasize WHEN, WHERE, HOW, WITH WHOM, or WHY an action was done, when it is already known that the action occurred in the past (both parties know the event has occurred). The structure is 主语 + 是 + [emphasized element] + 动词 + 的; 是 can often be dropped in affirmative sentences but the meaning remains the same. This structure is never used for future or actions that have not yet occurred — in this way it differs from the 了 [le] particle which indicates completed actions. The emphasized element is always placed between 是 [shì] and the verb, this is the most important information in the sentence.

chule-yiwai.intro_tr: The 除了...以外 [chúle...yǐwài] structure corresponds to 'besides' or 'outside of' in Turkish and is a fundamental pattern frequently encountered at HSK3 level. The most important characteristic of this structure is that it can be used in TWO DIFFERENT meanings: if 都/也是[dōu] is used in the second part of the sentence, it creates an 'excluding this, everything/everyone else' (exclusive) meaning; if 也[yě] or 还[hái] is used, it creates a 'in addition to this, along with this' (inclusive) meaning. The structure is formed as 除了[chúle] + noun/clause + 以外[yǐwài] and 以外[yǐwài] can usually be replaced with 之外[zhīwài] or 外[wài] alone. It can appear at the beginning of the sentence or after the subject; sometimes the 以外[yǐwài] part is omitted entirely and only 除了[chúle] is used. This page presents both meanings of the structure, its shortened forms, and a comparison with similar patterns in table format.

In inclusive meaning, both A and B are valid, one does not exclude the other — 除了[chúle] here functions like 'besides'.

bi-comparison-extended.title_tr: 比 Extended Comparison Structure (比...更 / 多了 / 一点儿)
bi-comparison-extended.intro_tr: After learning the basic comparison structure with 比 [bǐ] (A 比 B + adjective), this structure is expanded to indicate the SIZE and DEGREE of the difference. Adding 更 [gèng] or 还 [hái] BEFORE the adjective adds the meaning of "even more"; AFTER the adjective, 一点儿 [yìdiǎnr]/一些 [yìxiē] indicates "a bit more", 得多 [de duō]/多了 [duō le] indicates "much more", or a concrete number/quantity indicates "exactly how much". Absolute degree adverbs such as 很, 非常, 太 are ABSOLUTELY NOT used in these structures because 比 already carries a "degree" meaning. This page collects all suffixes that indicate the degree of difference, negative forms, and common mistakes in a single table.

tables.caption_tr: General Schema of the Extended 比 Structure
rows: 他比我更忙。[Tā bǐ wǒ gèng máng.] — O benden daha da meşgul.
daha da (更'ye yakın, biraz daha yumuşak/konuşma dili)
这个比那个还便宜。[Zhège bǐ nàge hái piányi.] — Bu ondan daha da ucuz.
我比你高一点儿。[Wǒ bǐ nǐ gāo yìdiǎnr.]
这里比那里安静得多。[Zhèlǐ bǐ nàlǐ ānjìng de duō.]
çok daha (büyük fark, konuşma dilinde yaygın)
今天比昨天热多了。[Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān rè duō le.]
他比我大两岁。[Tā bǐ wǒ dà liǎng suì.] — O benden iki yaş büyük.

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of Degree Suffixes: When to Use Which?
rows: 妹妹比姐姐矮一点儿。[Mèimei bǐ jiějie ǎi yìdiǎnr.]
Küçük kız kardeş büyük kız kardeşten biraz daha kısa.
hem yazı hem konuşma dilinde, biraz resmî
北京比我的家乡冷得多。[Běijīng bǐ wǒ de jiāxiāng lěng de duō.]
这个方法比以前的好多了。[Zhège fāngfǎ bǐ yǐqián de hǎo duō le.]
Bu yöntem öncekinden çok daha iyi.
这条河比那条河长五百米。[Zhè tiáo hé bǐ nà tiáo hé cháng wǔbǎi mǐ.]
Bu nehir o nehirden 500 metre daha uzun.
她比我更了解这里。[Tā bǐ wǒ gèng liǎojiě zhèlǐ.]
O burayı benden daha da iyi tanıyor.

tables.caption_tr: Negative and Question Forms
rows: A + 不比 [bù bǐ] + B + Sıfat
他不比我高。[Tā bù bǐ wǒ gāo.]
O benden yüksek değil (belki bana eşit ya da daha kısa).
'A, B'den daha az değildir' anlamına da gelebilir; net üstünlük iddia etmez.
A + 没有 [méiyǒu] + B + (那么/这么) + Sıfat
他没有我高。[Tā méiyǒu wǒ gāo.]
O benim kadar uzun değil (benden kısa).
不比'den daha net biçimde 'B'den az' anlamı verir; günlük dilde daha sık tercih edilir.
A + 比 + B + Sıfat + 多少 [duōshao]?
你比他大多少?[Nǐ bǐ tā dà duōshao?]
A + 比 + B + Sıfat + 吗?
这个比那个贵吗?[Zhège bǐ nàge guì ma?]

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: ✓ 我比他更高。 / 我比他高。
比 yapısında 很, 太, 非常, 挺 gibi mutlak derece zarfları KULLANILMAZ; bunların yerine 更 veya 还 kullanılır.
✓ 他比我高得多。 / 他比我高多了。
'Çok daha' anlamı için 非常多 değil, 得多 veya 多了 kullanılır.
一点儿/一些 mutlaka SIFATTAN SONRA gelir, önce değil.
✓ 我比他大很多。 / 我比他大好几岁。
Kesin sayı kullanılacaksa 很多 yerine doğrudan sayı (两岁, 三岁) ya da 好几 kullanılır; 很多岁 doğal değildir.
不比 zaten olumsuzdur, sıfatın önüne ayrıca 不 eklenmez.

examples.target: 我比他更高。
examples.reading: Wǒ bǐ tā gèng gāo.
examples.translation_tr: I am even taller than him. (he is already tall, but I am even taller than him)

examples.target: 今天比昨天冷多了。
examples.reading: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng duō le.
examples.translation_tr: Today is much colder than yesterday.

examples.target: 这件衣服比那件贵一点儿。
examples.reading: Zhè jiàn yīfu bǐ nà jiàn guì yìdiǎnr.
examples.translation_tr: This garment is a bit more expensive than that garment.

examples.target: 他比我大三岁。
examples.reading: Tā bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.translation_tr: He/She is three years older than me.

examples.target: 我的汉语水平比以前好得多。
examples.reading: Wǒ de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng bǐ yǐqián hǎo de duō.
examples.translation_tr: My Chinese is much better than before.

examples.target: 这个问题比那个问题还难。
examples.reading: Zhège wèntí bǐ nàge wèntí hái nán.
examples.translation_tr: This question is even more difficult than that question.

examples.target: 弟弟不比哥哥矮。
examples.reading: Dìdi bù bǐ gēge ǎi.
examples.translation_tr: The younger sibling is not shorter than the older sibling.

examples.target: 她跑得比我快一些。
examples.reading: Tā pǎo de bǐ wǒ kuài yìxiē.
examples.translation_tr: He/She runs a bit faster than me.

yuelaiyue.intro_tr: The pattern 越来越[yuèláiyuè] is used to express that a situation or quality gradually increases or changes over time; it corresponds to the Turkish expression 'gradually, increasingly...' The structure is very simple: 越来越 + Adjective or 越来越 + Verb (usually emotion/state verbs), and it never takes inflection. The 是 verb is not used; the adjective comes directly after 越来越. The 了[le] added to the end of the sentence usually reinforces that this change continues, but it is not mandatory. This pattern should not be confused with the 越...越...[yuè...yuè...] structure which compares the same topic between two variables.

tables.caption_tr: 越来越 Basic Structure
footnotes_tr: The 是 verb is not used in this structure; the adjective comes directly after 越来越.

tables.caption_tr: Negation with 越来越
rows: 越来越 + 少 (doğal olumsuz anlam)
footnotes_tr: 越来越 itself is never negated directly with 不 or 没 (❌ 不越来越); negation always comes before the adjective/verb.
The structure '越来越不 + Adjective' expresses the opposite meaning of the adjective, e.g. 好 (good) → 不好 (bad).

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of 越来越 and 越...越...
rows: Zaman geçtikçe tek bir durumun kendiliğinden artışını anlatır
İki değişken/eylem arasındaki bağıntılı artışı anlatır (A arttıkça B de artar)
Nǐ yuè shuō wǒ yuè bù dǒng.
Sen anlattıkça ben daha az anlıyorum.
O pratik yaptıkça daha iyi oluyor.
footnotes_tr: In 越来越, a single subject/situation changes over time; in 越...越..., two related elements usually increase together.

tables.caption_tr: Frequently Used 越来越 Patterns
Usage Together with 随着
rows: 随着经济的发展，生活越来越好。
Suízhe jīngjì de fāzhǎn, shēnghuó yuèláiyuè hǎo.
Ekonominin gelişmesiyle birlikte, hayat gitgide iyileşiyor.
随着时间的推移，... 越来越 ...
随着时间的推移，他越来越成熟。
Suízhe shíjiān de tuīyí, tā yuèláiyuè chéngshú.
footnotes_tr: The preposition 随着, when used together with 越来越, clearly specifies the reason for the change; it is common in formal and written language.

examples.target: 天气越来越冷了。
examples.reading: Tiānqì yuèláiyuè lěng le.
examples.translation_tr: The weather is getting gradually colder.
examples.note_tr: The 了 at the end of the sentence emphasizes that the change continues/is intensified; in sentences with 越来越, 了 is often added but not mandatory.

examples.target: 我的汉语越来越好。
examples.reading: Wǒ de Hànyǔ yuèláiyuè hǎo.
examples.translation_tr: My Chinese is gradually improving.

examples.target: 城市里的车越来越多。
examples.reading: Chéngshì lǐ de chē yuèláiyuè duō.
examples.translation_tr: The cars in the city are increasingly multiplying.
examples.note_tr: 多 and 少 come directly after 越来越 as adjectives; 是 is not used.

examples.target: 他越来越喜欢中国菜。
examples.reading: Tā yuèláiyuè xǐhuan Zhōngguó cài.
examples.translation_tr: He/She increasingly loves Chinese food more and more.
examples.note_tr: Emotion/state verbs like 喜欢 can also be graded with 越来越.

examples.target: 随着年龄的增长，他越来越懂事。
examples.reading: Suízhe niánlíng de zēngzhǎng, tā yuèláiyuè dǒngshì.
examples.translation_tr: As he/she grows older, he/she becomes increasingly more understanding.
examples.note_tr: When used together with 随着, the cause-effect relationship is more clearly emphasized.

examples.target: 这个问题越来越复杂了。
examples.reading: Zhège wèntí yuèláiyuè fùzá le.
examples.translation_tr: This problem is becoming increasingly complicated.

examples.target: 她的中文说得越来越流利。
examples.reading: Tā de Zhōngwén shuō de yuèláiyuè liúlì.
examples.translation_tr: His/Her Chinese is becoming increasingly fluent.
examples.note_tr: When used together with the 得 complement, 得 comes after the verb, then 越来越 + adjective is added.

examples.target: 冬天越来越冷，夏天越来越热。
examples.reading: Dōngtiān yuèláiyuè lěng, xiàtiān yuèláiyuè rè.
examples.translation_tr: Winter is getting gradually colder, summer is getting gradually warmer.
examples.note_tr: Opposite changes can be expressed by using multiple 越来越 in the same sentence.

weile-purpose.title_tr: 为了 (wèile): "for (the purpose of), with the aim of"
weile-purpose.intro_tr: 为了[wèile] is a preposition used to indicate the purpose or goal of an action and corresponds to the Turkish phrase "for (the purpose of), with the aim of". It can be used at the beginning of a sentence or immediately after the subject; the part that follows usually describes the action taken to achieve that goal. After 为了, a single noun, a verb phrase, or an entire sentence can follow. It should not be confused with 因为[yīnwèi], which indicates cause: 为了 describes a goal that is future-oriented and has not yet been realized, while 因为 explains a reason that already exists or is present. The most important rule for zero-level students is that 为了 always appears at the beginning of the part that indicates the purpose, and the action taken to achieve that goal comes after it.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Sentence Structure: Where is 为了[wèile] Used?
rows: Sağlık için her gün spor yapıyorum.
Ben sağlık için her gün spor yapıyorum.
为了 + Fiil Öbeği, Özne + Eylem
为了学好汉语,他每天练习。
Wèile xuéhǎo Hànyǔ, tā měitiān liànxí.
Çinceyi iyi öğrenmek için her gün pratik yapıyor.
为了 + Amaç, Özne + 要/应该/会 + Eylem
为了考试,你应该好好复习。
Wèile kǎoshì, nǐ yīnggāi hǎohǎo fùxí.
为了 + Olumsuz Fiil (不 + V), Özne + Eylem
为了不迟到,他打车去了。
Wèile bù chídào, tā dǎchē qù le.
footnotes_tr: The purpose section beginning with 为了 is separated by a comma; the second half of the sentence describes the concrete action taken to achieve that goal.
为了 can be used both at the beginning of a sentence and immediately after the subject; the meaning does not change, only the emphasis shifts slightly.

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of 为了[wèile] (purpose) and 因为[yīnwèi] (reason)
rows: Genellikle tek başına kullanılır, 所以 gerekmez
Genellikle 所以[suǒyǐ] ile birlikte kullanılır
İleriye dönük: henüz gerçekleşmemiş bir hedef
Geriye dönük: zaten var olan bir durum/sebep
为了减肥,她不吃甜食。 (Kilo vermek için tatlı yemiyor.)
因为她想减肥,所以不吃甜食。 (Kilo vermek istediği için tatlı yemiyor.)
footnotes_tr: In a 为了 sentence, the purpose has not yet been realized; the action is performed to achieve that goal.
In a 因为...所以... sentence, the reason already exists and the consequence arises from it.

tables.caption_tr: The Difference Between 为了[wèile] and 为[wèi]
rows: Konuşma ve yazı dilinde çok yaygın, günlük ifadeler
Daha çok resmî/kalıplaşmış ifadelerde, tek başına az kullanılır
İsim, fiil öbeği veya tüm bir cümle
Genellikle kısa bir isim veya sabit kalıp
İki heceli, amaç anlamını daha açık ve vurgulu belirtir
Tek heceli, daha kısa, daha resmî bir hava taşır
为了大家的健康,请戴口罩。 (Herkesin sağlığı için lütfen maske takın.)
Günlük konuşmada güvenle 为了 kullanılabilir
为 çoğunlukla sabit kalıplarda ezbere öğrenilir, üretici kullanım zor
footnotes_tr: At the beginner level, it is safer to always use 为了 instead of 为; 为 is learned at an advanced level with formal patterns.

tables.caption_tr: Frequently Used 为了 Patterns
rows: 为了未来 (Wèile wèilái) — Gelecek için
为了学习 (Wèile xuéxí) — Öğrenmek için
为了 + amaç, 特意/专门 + eylem
为了看你,我专门来了。 (Seni görmek için özellikle geldim.)
他这样做是为了帮助你。 (Böyle yapmasının amacı sana yardım etmektir.)
为了安全起见,请系好安全带。 (Güvenlik amacıyla lütfen emniyet kemerinizi bağlayın.)
footnotes_tr: The '为了...起见' pattern is frequently seen in formal written language and in warning/instruction sentences; it is sufficient to recognize it at zero level.

examples.target: 为了健康,我每天运动。
examples.reading: Wèile jiànkāng, wǒ měitiān yùndòng.
examples.translation_tr: I exercise every day for my health.

examples.target: 为了学好汉语,他每天听录音。
examples.reading: Wèile xuéhǎo Hànyǔ, tā měitiān tīng lùyīn.
examples.translation_tr: He/She listens to audio recordings every day in order to learn Chinese well.

examples.target: 她为了买房子努力工作。
examples.reading: Tā wèile mǎi fángzi nǔlì gōngzuò.
examples.translation_tr: He/She works hard in order to buy a house.

examples.target: 为了不迟到,我今天早点儿起床了。
examples.reading: Wèile bù chídào, wǒ jīntiān zǎodiǎnr qǐchuáng le.
examples.translation_tr: I woke up early today in order not to be late.

examples.target: 我们为了环保应该少用塑料袋。
examples.reading: Wǒmen wèile huánbǎo yīnggāi shǎo yòng sùliàodài.
examples.translation_tr: We should reduce plastic bag usage in order to protect the environment.

examples.target: 为了见到你,我坐了十个小时的飞机。
examples.reading: Wèile jiàndào nǐ, wǒ zuòle shí ge xiǎoshí de fēijī.
examples.translation_tr: I traveled by plane for ten hours in order to be able to see you.

examples.target: 他为了孩子的未来搬到了大城市。
examples.reading: Tā wèile háizi de wèilái bāndàole dà chéngshì.
examples.translation_tr: He/She moved to a big city for his/her child's future.

examples.target: 为了让父母放心,她常常打电话回家。
examples.reading: Wèile ràng fùmǔ fàngxīn, tā chángcháng dǎ diànhuà huí jiā.
examples.translation_tr: He/She calls home frequently in order to put his/her family at ease.

dui-coverb.title_tr: 对 (duì) Preposition: Directional Preposition with the Meaning 'Toward/Against, About'
dui-coverb.intro_tr: 对 [duì] is one of the most frequently used prepositions (coverbs) in Chinese and its basic meaning is 'toward/against, about, ...according to'. In a sentence, it is generally used in the order "Subject + 对 + Object + Predicate" and indicates whom/what an emotion, attitude, or effect is directed toward. 对 can also be used independently as an adjective meaning 'correct' (你说得对); it is important not to confuse these two usages. For a beginner-level student, the most critical point is understanding that 对 is not a VERB but a PREPOSITION and that a real predicate (verb/adjective) must necessarily follow it.

tables.caption_tr: 对 (duì) Preposition: Basic Sentence Structure
rows: 我对这个电影很感兴趣。[Wǒ duì zhège diànyǐng hěn gǎn xìngqù.]
Bu filme karşı çok ilgi duyuyorum.
Özne + 对 + Nesne + 很/不 + Sıfat
妈妈对我很关心。[Māma duì wǒ hěn guānxīn.]
Annem beni çok önemsiyor (bana karşı ilgili).
Özne + 对 + Nesne + 有/没有 + İsim
锻炼对健康有好处。[Duànliàn duì jiànkāng yǒu hǎochù.]
对年轻人来说，工作很重要。[Duì niánqīngrén láishuō, gōngzuò hěn zhòngyào.]
Gençler için (gençlere göre) iş çok önemlidir.
对公司而言，这是个好机会。[Duì gōngsī éryán, zhè shì gè hǎo jīhuì.]
Şirket açısından bu iyi bir fırsattır.

tables.caption_tr: Common Idiomatic Expressions Used with 对 (duì)
rows: 他对音乐很感兴趣。[Tā duì yīnyuè hěn gǎn xìngqù.] (Müziğe çok ilgi duyuyor.)
运动对减肥有帮助。[Yùndòng duì jiǎnféi yǒu bāngzhù.] (Spor kilo vermeye yardımcıdır.)
抽烟对身体有坏处。[Chōuyān duì shēntǐ yǒu huàichù.] (Sigara sağlığa zararlıdır.)
健康对每个人都重要。[Jiànkāng duì měi gè rén dōu zhòngyào.] (Sağlık herkes için önemlidir.)
我对这个城市不太了解。[Wǒ duì zhège chéngshì bú tài liǎojiě.] (Bu şehri pek tanımıyorum.)
老板对我的工作很满意。[Lǎobǎn duì wǒ de gōngzuò hěn mǎnyì.] (Patron işimden memnun.)
医生要对病人负责。[Yīshēng yào duì bìngrén fùzé.] (Doktor hastadan sorumlu olmalıdır.)
他对客人很热情。[Tā duì kèrén hěn rèqíng.] (Misafirlere karşı çok sıcakkanlı.)
父母对孩子很严格。[Fùmǔ duì háizi hěn yángé.] (Ebeveynler çocuklarına karşı katı.)

tables.caption_tr: Different Usage Types of the Word 对 (duì)
rows: 他对我很热情。[Tā duì wǒ hěn rèqíng.]
En yaygın kullanım; nesneden sonra gerçek yüklem gelir.
你说得对。[Nǐ shuō de duì.]
Fiilden sonra 得 ile derece tümleci olarak sık kullanılır.
Tek başına sabit bir kalıptır, parçalara ayrılmaz.
对了，你吃饭了吗？[Duìle, nǐ chīfàn le ma?]

tables.caption_tr: 对 vs 对于 vs 跟/和: Difference Between Confused Prepositions
rows: Duygu, tutum, etki bildirir (kişi veya konu)
我对他很满意。[Wǒ duì tā hěn mǎnyì.]
Daha resmî, genellikle cümle başında konu belirtir
对于这个问题，我们要认真讨论。[Duìyú zhège wèntí, wǒmen yào rènzhēn tǎolùn.]
Kişiler hakkında duygu bildirirken kullanılmaz, konu/mesele içindir.
我跟他一起去。[Wǒ gēn tā yìqǐ qù.]
对 duygu yönelimini, 跟/和 beraberliği anlatır — karıştırılmamalı.
我给他打电话。[Wǒ gěi tā dǎ diànhuà.]
对 tutum/duygu, 给 ise somut bir eylemin alıcısını gösterir.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes in Using 对 (duì)
rows: 我对他喜欢。 [Wǒ duì tā xǐhuan.] (yanlış)
喜欢 doğrudan geçişli bir fiildir, 对 ile kullanılmaz; nesne doğrudan fiilden sonra gelir.
对我来说，这个很难。[Duì wǒ láishuō, zhège hěn nán.]
'Bence/benim için' derken 对 tek başına yetmez, 来说 veya 而言 eklenmelidir.
他对我很好。[Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo.]
跟 beraberlik bildirir ('birlikte'), tutum anlatmak için 对 kullanılmalıdır.
运动身体有好处。 (对 unutulmuş)
运动对身体有好处。[Yùndòng duì shēntǐ yǒu hǎochù.]
对 olmadan nesnenin etkilendiği alan belirtilmez, cümle eksik/anlamsız olur.

examples.note_tr: 对 + object (中国文化) + 感兴趣 pattern: 'to be interested in...'

examples.target: 他对我很好。

examples.translation_tr: He/She is very good toward me (behaves very well).
examples.note_tr: 对 + person + 很 + adjective: expresses one's attitude toward someone.

examples.target: 这件事对他影响很大。
examples.reading: Zhè jiàn shì duì tā yǐngxiǎng hěn dà.
examples.translation_tr: This event affected him/her greatly (had a great impact on him/her).
examples.note_tr: A variation of the 对...有影响 pattern.

examples.target: 运动对身体有好处。
examples.reading: Yùndòng duì shēntǐ yǒu hǎochù.
examples.translation_tr: Doing sports is beneficial for the body.
examples.note_tr: 对...有好处: 'to be beneficial for...'

examples.target: 老师对学生很严格。
examples.reading: Lǎoshī duì xuésheng hěn yángé.
examples.translation_tr: The teacher is very strict/severe toward students.

examples.target: 对不起，我来晚了。
examples.reading: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ lái wǎn le.
examples.translation_tr: I apologize, I came late.
examples.note_tr: 对不起 is a fixed apology expression, where 对 is not used independently as a preposition here.

examples.target: 对我来说，学汉语不容易。
examples.reading: Duì wǒ láishuō, xué Hànyǔ bù róngyì.

examples.note_tr: 对 + person + 来说: pattern for expressing opinion with the meaning 'according to someone, for someone'

examples.target: 你说得对。
examples.reading: Nǐ shuō de duì.
examples.translation_tr: You are saying it correctly.
examples.note_tr: Here 对 is used as an adjective meaning 'correct', not as a preposition — don't confuse it!

bei-passive-basic.intro_tr: 被 (bèi) is the most common marker used to form passive voice sentences in Chinese and adds the meaning of "... by ... -ed/-ized". While Turkish passive voice uses verb suffixes (ending in -il, -in), in Chinese the subject is placed at the beginning of the sentence, the agent (the one performing the action) is optionally specified after 被, and the verb is never left bare — it must be followed by 了, a resultative complement, or some other completing element. Traditionally, 被 is most often used in negative or undesired events (such as "was stolen", "was broken", "was fired"), but in modern colloquial speech it can also be used comfortably in neutral events. This structure can be thought of as a mirror image of the 把 (bǎ) structure: while 把 brings the object to the front and applies the verb to it, 被 emphasizes the action that befalls the subject.

tables.caption_tr: 被 Structure's Basic Sentence Schema
rows: Eylemin sonucunu üstlenen kişi/nesne; cümlenin en başında yer alır.
Belirtilmezse 被 doğrudan fiile bağlanır: 被 + Fiil.
Çince'de çıplak (tek başına) tek heceli fiil genelde kullanılmaz.
了, 走, 破, 好 gibi bir unsur fiile eklenmelidir; aksi halde cümle eksik sayılır.

tables.caption_tr: Expressing the Same Meaning with Three Sentence Structures: SVO, 把, 被
footnotes_tr: 把 emphasizes the result of the verb on the object; 被 emphasizes the action that the subject undergoes. Neither leaves the verb bare.

tables.caption_tr: 被 Structure's Negative and Question Forms
rows: 没(有) daima 被'den ÖNCE gelir; 不 kullanılmaz (tamamlanmış olaylarda)
Zhège mìmì bú huì bèi fāxiàn.
Soru sözcüğü ajan konumuna (被'den hemen sonra) gelir
被 yapısıyla KULLANILMAZ; bunun yerine 吗 tercih edilir

tables.caption_tr: Common Verb + Complement Patterns Used with 被
rows: Shū bèi fàng zài zhuōzi shàng le.
Qián bèi piànzǒu le yíwàn kuài.

tables.caption_tr: 被 vs 叫 vs 让: Usage Differences in Colloquial Speech
rows: Hem yazı hem konuşma dilinde yaygın
东西被拿走了。(Dōngxi bèi názǒu le.)
东西叫他拿走了。(Dōngxi jiào tā názǒu le.)
东西让他拿走了。(Dōngxi ràng tā názǒu le.)
footnotes_tr: 叫 and 让 originate as causative verbs meaning 'to cause/make (someone do something)'; therefore omitting the agent is not natural. For details, see the 'Passive Voice Complete Coverage' topic.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes and Correct Usage
rows: 鱼被猫吃了。 (Yú bèi māo chī le.)
Fiil çıplak bırakılamaz; 了 veya bir tümleç eklenmelidir.
我没被批评。 (Wǒ méi bèi pīpíng.)
Geçmişte gerçekleşmemiş olayların olumsuzlanmasında 不 değil 没 kullanılır.
被 yapısı V-不-V soru formunu almaz; 吗 kullanılmalıdır.
书被我拿走了。 / 我把书拿走了。
被 ve 把 aynı cümlede üst üste, aynı nesne için kullanılmaz; ikisinden yalnızca biri seçilir.

examples.target: 我的钱包被小偷偷了。
examples.reading: Wǒ de qiánbāo bèi xiǎotōu tōu le.
examples.translation_tr: My wallet was stolen by a thief.
examples.note_tr: The agent (小偷) is specified; 了 serves as a necessary complement after the verb.

examples.target: 杯子被打破了。
examples.reading: Bēizi bèi dǎpò le.
examples.translation_tr: The glass was broken.
examples.note_tr: The agent is unknown/irrelevant and has been omitted: 被 is attached directly to the verb.

examples.target: 这本书被他借走了。
examples.reading: Zhè běn shū bèi tā jièzǒu le.
examples.translation_tr: This book was borrowed by him/her.
examples.note_tr: The verb is completed with 借走 as a resultative complement; a bare verb could not be used.

examples.target: 作业被老师检查了。
examples.reading: Zuòyè bèi lǎoshī jiǎnchá le.
examples.translation_tr: The homework was checked by the teacher.

examples.target: 他被公司开除了。
examples.reading: Tā bèi gōngsī kāichú le.
examples.translation_tr: He/She was fired by the company.
examples.note_tr: 被 is traditionally often used in negative/undesired events.

examples.target: 苹果被我吃了。
examples.reading: Píngguǒ bèi wǒ chī le.
examples.translation_tr: I ate the apple (the apple was eaten by me).
examples.note_tr: In modern Chinese it can also be used in positive/neutral events.

examples.target: 门没被关上。
examples.reading: Mén méi bèi guānshàng.
examples.translation_tr: The door was not closed.
examples.note_tr: The negation 没 always comes before 被, and 不 is never used (in past events).

examples.target: 他的电脑被谁修好了?
examples.reading: Tā de diànnǎo bèi shéi xiūhǎo le?
examples.translation_tr: Who repaired his/her computer?
examples.note_tr: The question word 谁 is placed in the agent position, that is, immediately after 被.

yue-yue.intro_tr: The structure 越...越... (yuè...yuè...) expresses that as one situation increases or changes, another situation also increases proportionally to it; it corresponds to the Turkish pattern '...-dıkça ...' (the more...the more...). Two 越s are used consecutively in the sentence: the first 越 indicates what increases (the condition/cause), and the second 越 indicates the resulting consequence. This structure can be used both with verbs (越学越会 - the more one studies, the better one learns) and with adjectives (越冷越好 - the colder the better), and the subject typically appears at the beginning of the structure, before both 越s. It should not be confused with 越来越 (increasingly...), which describes a one-directional change over time; because in the 越...越... structure two variables increase together in relation to each other, whereas in 越来越 a single situation increases over time. This pattern is used very frequently in everyday conversation and especially appears in fixed expressions like 越多越好, 越快越好.

tables.caption_tr: Components of the Basic Structure
rows: Cümlenin öznesi, yapının en başında yer alır
Artan/değişen ilk durumu bildirir (fiil ya da sıfat)
Birinci duruma bağlı olarak ortaya çıkan sonucu bildirir
他越学越会。(Tā yuè xué yuè huì.)
İki 越 parçası bir araya gelir, özne genelde en başta kalır
footnotes_tr: The subject can sometimes be placed between the two 越s: 越学他越会 is used less frequently; the most common word order is subject + 越 A + 越 B.

tables.caption_tr: Usage with Different Types of Words
rows: Hava ne kadar soğuk olursa o kadar iyi (örn. kayak için)
yuè wǎn yuè shuì bu zháo
Para ne kadar çok olursa o kadar mutlu

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of 越...越... with Similar Structures
rows: İki değişken birbirine bağlı olarak birlikte artar
越忙越累 (yuè máng yuè lèi)
Karşılıklı ilişki: A arttıkça B de artar
天气越来越冷 (tiānqì yuèláiyuè lěng)
Tek değişken vardır, zaman içindeki değişimi anlatır, ikinci bir 越 yoktur
Bir durumu vurgulamak, çoğu zaman beklenmedik/inatçı bir tepkiyi anlatmak için
你越是不让我做，我越想做
Vurgu katmak için 是 eklenir; genelde ters/direnç anlamı taşır

tables.caption_tr: Negation, 了, and Usage Restrictions
rows: 不/没 genellikle sonuç (ikinci) kısmına eklenir
越解释越不清楚 (yuè jiěshì yuè bù qīngchu) - açıkladıkça daha da anlaşılmaz oluyor
Cümle sonuna 了 eklenerek değişimin gerçekleştiği/sürdüğü vurgulanır
雨越下越大了 (yǔ yuè xià yuè dà le) - yağmur giderek şiddetlendi
越...越... bir gözlem/sonuç yapısıdır, emir veya rica cümlesi kurmaz
(越努力越好 doğru ama '越努力吧' gibi emir formu yanlıştır)
吗 veya 呢 cümle sonuna eklenerek soru yapılabilir
是不是越吃越胖呢？ (yediğin kadar mı şişmanlıyorsun?)

tables.caption_tr: Frequently Used Set Expressions
rows: Ne kadar çok olursa o kadar iyi
Ne kadar hızlı olursa o kadar iyi
Ne kadar erken olursa o kadar iyi
Ne kadar basit olursa o kadar iyi
Ne kadar büyük olursa o kadar iyi
footnotes_tr: These patterns are often used alone as short answers: 要多少？—越多越好！(How much do you want? — The more the better!)

examples.target: 你越努力，越幸运。
examples.reading: Nǐ yuè nǔlì, yuè xìngyùn.
examples.translation_tr: The more effort you make, the luckier you become.

examples.target: 他越说越激动。

examples.translation_tr: The more he/she talks, the more excited he/she becomes.

examples.target: 雨越下越大了。
examples.reading: Yǔ yuè xià yuè dà le.
examples.translation_tr: The more it rained, the more intense it became.

examples.target: 这本书越看越有意思。
examples.reading: Zhè běn shū yuè kàn yuè yǒu yìsi.
examples.translation_tr: The more I read this book, the more interesting it seems.

examples.target: 我们越聊越晚。
examples.reading: Wǒmen yuè liáo yuè wǎn.
examples.translation_tr: The more we chatted, the more time passed.

examples.target: 东西越便宜越好。
examples.reading: Dōngxi yuè piányi yuè hǎo.
examples.translation_tr: The cheaper the items, the better.

examples.target: 他越忙越没有时间休息。

double-object-verbs.title_tr: Double Object Verbs (给, 教, 送, 问)
double-object-verbs.intro_tr: In Chinese, some verbs can take two objects at the same time: one "to whom" (indirect object, usually a person), the other "what" (direct object, usually a thing or topic). The most common examples of these verbs are 给[gěi] (to give), 教[jiāo] (to teach), 送[sòng] (to gift/send), and 问[wèn] (to ask). The basic rule is very simple: immediately after the verb comes FIRST the person (to whom), THEN the thing (what) — you need to memorize the order so you don't confuse it with the Turkish dative case ending "-e". This structure appears very frequently at HSK3 level and is one of the cornerstones of everyday conversation. In the tables below, the structure, verb list, negation/question forms, and common mistakes are shown in detail.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Sentence Formula: Subject + Verb + Person (IO) + Thing (DO)
footnotes_tr: Complete sentence: 我给你一本书。 (wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū) — 'I'm giving you a book.'
ORDER IS VERY IMPORTANT: first the PERSON, then the THING comes. This order is the same as 'to you the book' in Turkish, it cannot be reversed.

tables.caption_tr: Most Frequently Used Double Object Verbs
rows: 他给我一杯茶。[tā gěi wǒ yì bēi chá] — O bana bir bardak çay veriyor.
她教我英语。[tā jiāo wǒ Yīngyǔ] — O bana İngilizce öğretiyor.
我送她一朵花。[wǒ sòng tā yì duǒ huā] — Ona bir çiçek veriyorum.
他问我一个问题。[tā wèn wǒ yí gè wèntí] — O bana bir soru soruyor.
我告诉你一个秘密。[wǒ gàosu nǐ yí gè mìmì] — Sana bir sır söylüyorum.
我还他一本书。[wǒ huán tā yì běn shū] — Ona bir kitap geri veriyorum.
他借我一百块钱。[tā jiè wǒ yìbǎi kuài qián] — O bana yüz yuan ödünç verdi.
我寄他一封信。[wǒ jì tā yì fēng xìn] — Ona bir mektup gönderiyorum.

tables.caption_tr: Complete Conjugation with the 给 Verb: Affirmative / Negative / Question / Past
rows: wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū
nǐ gěi wǒ yì běn shū ma?
nǐ gěi bu gěi wǒ qián?
Bana para verecek misin vermeyecek misin?
wǒ gěi le tā yì běn shū
footnotes_tr: 不 and 没 always come BEFORE the VERB, not before the person or thing objects.
The 了 perfective aspect suffix is attached immediately after the verb: 给了[gěi le], 送了[sòng le].

tables.caption_tr: Verb-Specific Special Uses and Extended Structures
rows: 妈妈教我游泳。[māma jiāo wǒ yóuyǒng] — Annem bana yüzmeyi öğretiyor.
DO burada bir isim değil, bir fiil (游泳) olabilir.
我送你回家。[wǒ sòng nǐ huí jiā] — Seni eve bırakıyorum.
DO burada bir yer/yön ifadesi olabilir, eşya değil.
我问老师一个问题。[wǒ wèn lǎoshī yí gè wèntí] — Öğretmene bir soru soruyorum.
İkinci nesne genelde 问题[wèntí] gibi soyut bir 'konu' olur.
他给我打电话。[tā gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà] — Bana telefon ediyor.
Burada 给 asıl fiil 打电话'dan önce gelen bir edattır, çift nesne yapısı değildir.

tables.caption_tr: Alternative Word Order: Verb + Thing (DO) + 给 + Person (IO)
rows: wǒ sòng nǐ yì běn shū
wǒ sòng yì běn shū gěi nǐ
Bir kitabı sana veriyorum. (aynı anlam, DO vurgulanır)
tā huán wǒ yìbǎi kuài qián
O bana yüz yuan geri verdi.
tā huán yìbǎi kuài qián gěi wǒ
O yüz yuanı bana geri verdi.
footnotes_tr: This alternative structure is particularly common with verbs like 送, 还, 寄, 交; it is not often used with 教 and 问 verbs.
The standard order is more common in everyday speech; the 给-pattern order is preferred when the object is to be emphasized.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: Kişi (IO) her zaman şeyden (DO) önce gelmelidir.
我不给一本书你不。 / 我给你不一本书。
不/没 fiilden önce gelir, iki nesnenin arasına asla girmez.
İki nesne arasında 的 kullanılmaz, doğrudan yan yana gelirler.
Kişi (IO) her zaman ilk nesne konumunda olmalı, beceri/konu (DO) ondan sonra gelir.
问 fiilinde de kişi önce, soru/konu sonra gelir.

resultative-complements.title_tr: Resultative Complements (完, 好, 到, 见, 懂, 错)
resultative-complements.intro_tr: In Chinese, to indicate not just that an action was performed, but what the result was, a second character (resultative complement) is added immediately after the verb; this pair behaves like a single word and nothing can be inserted between them. In this lesson you will learn the six most commonly used resultative complements: 完[wán] (to complete), 好[hǎo] (to complete successfully/be ready), 到[dào] (to reach a target/succeed), 见[jiàn] (to perceive through the senses), 懂[dǒng] (to understand), and 错[cuò] (to do wrongly). For negation, 没[méi] rather than 不[bù] is used because the issue is whether the action was accomplished or not. Resultative complements are typically used together with 了[le], and if there is an object it comes after the complement. Because this structure appears very frequently at HSK3 level, memorizing the six complements and their typical verb pairings is of great benefit.

tables.caption_tr: Table 1: Six Basic Resultative Complements
rows: Duyu organıyla farkına varma, genellikle istem dışı
footnotes_tr: All resultative complements are written attached to the verb, and nothing can be inserted between the verb and the complement (including 了, which comes AFTER the complement).

tables.caption_tr: Table 2: Affirmative, Negative, and Question Structures
rows: 你吃完了吗?[Nǐ chīwán le ma?]
你吃完了没有?[Nǐ chīwán le méiyǒu?]
footnotes_tr: In simple negation, 不 is never used, only 没(有) is used: 我不吃完 is INCORRECT.
Potential (capability) complements formed with 得/不 are a separate topic; they are shown here only for comparative purposes.

tables.caption_tr: Table 3: Commonly Used Verb + Complement Combinations
Table 4: Word Order When an Object is Present (Where Does 了 Go?)
rows: 我看完了。[Wǒ kànwán le.] — Okuyup bitirdim.
我看完了这本书。[Wǒ kànwán le zhè běn shū.] — Bu kitabı okuyup bitirdim.
我看完这本书了。[Wǒ kànwán zhè běn shū le.] — Bu kitabı okuyup bitirdim (artık bitti).
我没看完这本书。[Wǒ méi kànwán zhè běn shū.] — Bu kitabı okuyup bitiremedim.
footnotes_tr: Two instances of 了 are not used together in the same sentence (Verb+Complement+了+Object+了 is INCORRECT).

tables.caption_tr: Table 5: Frequently Confused Trio — The Difference Between 到 / 见 / 懂 (especially with 看 and 听)
rows: Hedefe fiilen ulaşmak/başarmak; soyut veya somut sonuç
找到了[zhǎodào le] — aradı ve buldu
看到/听到 çoğu zaman 看见/听见 ile neredeyse eş anlamlıdır
Duyu organıyla anlık, çoğu zaman istemsiz algılama
见 sadece 看, 听, 闻 gibi algı fiilleriyle kullanılır
看懂了[kàndǒng le] — okudu ve içeriğini anladı
看到/看见 sadece görmeyi ifade eder, anlamayı ifade etmez
footnotes_tr: Example: 我看到黑板上的字,但是看不懂。[Wǒ kàndào hēibǎn shang de zì, dànshì kànbudǒng.] — I saw the writing on the blackboard but couldn't understand it (this sentence clearly shows the difference between 到/懂).

approximate-numbers.title_tr: Approximate Numbers (几, 多, 左右, 大概)
approximate-numbers.intro_tr: In Chinese, several different "approximate number" tools are used to express numbers that are not exactly known or are not important: 几[jǐ] is generally used for uncertain numbers less than 10 (several, how many), 多[duō] is used to express a little more than the stated number (surplus/fraction), 左右[zuǒyòu] is used for the meaning "around" that encompasses both above and below a number, and 大概[dàgài] is used as an adverb that emphasizes the speaker's own estimate "probably, approximately". The POSITION of these four structures within a sentence is different, and some (e.g., 多) change position depending on the type of number; therefore the most common errors are position errors. On this page, the pattern, position, and differences of each structure are summarized in tables.

yinggai-dei-modals.title_tr: 应该 / 得(děi) / 必须: Necessity Modals
yinggai-dei-modals.intro_tr: 应该[yīnggāi], 得[děi] and 必须[bìxū] are three fundamental necessity modals in Chinese meaning 'to need, should/must'; however, they differ in their degree of formality, context of use, and negative forms. 应该[yīnggāi] expresses a moral or logical recommendation/expectation ('logically it should be so'); 得[děi], used only in spoken language, expresses a personal/situational necessity; 必须[bìxū], on the other hand, expresses a strong necessity of the nature of a rule, law, or definite condition and is more formal. The most critical point is that the negative forms of these three modals are irregular: the negative of 得[děi] is never 不得[bùdé], nor is the negative of 必须[bìxū] 不必须 — instead, 不用[búyòng] or 不必[búbì] ('no need') is used for both. On this page, the comparison of these three modals, their negative forms, contexts of use, and common mistakes are summarized in tables.

duration-complement.title_tr: Duration Complement (学了三年汉语) — Expressing Time Duration
duration-complement.intro_tr: Duration complement (时量补语) is a structure used after a verb to indicate how long an action lasts — it corresponds to expressions like "for three years", "for half an hour" in Turkish. The basic pattern is Verb + 了 + Duration; when an action is used together with an object, either the verb must be repeated or the duration-object must be combined with 的. Adding a second 了 at the end of the sentence indicates that the action is still continuing, while using it without indicates the action has ended. Since this topic appears very frequently at HSK3 level, it is important that you distinguish the three patterns well (verb repetition, 的 combination, pronoun object).

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure: Position of Duration Complement in the Sentence
rows: Özne + Fiil + 了 + Süre + 了
Özne + Süre + 没 + Fiil + 了
Tā sān nián méi huí jiā le.
Üç yıldır eve dönmedi (olumsuz, süregelen durum).
footnotes_tr: If a second 了 is added, it is understood that the action is still continuing now; if it is not added, generally the action has been completed or the context determines.

tables.caption_tr: Frequently Used Duration Expressions
Usage with Object: Three Basic Patterns

Ö + V + 了 + Süre + 的 + Nesne

Wǒ rènshi tā sān nián le.
footnotes_tr: If the object is a personal pronoun (他, 她, 它, 你, 我) or a proper noun, the verb is not repeated, and the duration comes directly after the object.
Pattern 2 (with '的') is preferred more in written language and formal narration; Pattern 1 is most common in everyday speech.

jiran-jiu.intro_tr: The 既然...就... pattern corresponds to the "since... then..." structure in Turkish and is used to express a conclusion, suggestion, or decision based on a situation that both the speaker and listener already know or that is evident. 既然[jìrán] introduces a known/realized situation in the first sentence, while 就[jiù] provides the logical conclusion or suggestion based on this situation in the second sentence. Unlike the 因为...所以... structure, 既然...就... does not present new information; it specifies what should be done based on an existing fact, which is why it mostly appears in advisory, suggestion, decision, or rhetorical question sentences. 既然 can be placed at the beginning of the sentence or immediately after the subject; in the second sentence, 就 always comes after the subject and before the verb, and is almost never omitted in this pattern.

que-contrast.intro_tr: The word 却 (què) in Chinese is an ADVERB that emphasizes an unexpected or contrary situation — not a CONJUNCTION like 但是 (dànshì) or 可是 (kěshì). It carries the meanings "but, however, yet, on the other hand" in Turkish, but unlike conjunctions, it cannot appear at the beginning of a sentence; it must come AFTER THE SUBJECT and BEFORE THE VERB or ADJECTIVE. 却 usually describes a result that contradicts or negates an expectation or normal logic set up in the previous sentence. Very often it is used together with 但是 or 虽然 to emphasize the contrast twice (但是...却..., 虽然...却...), but it can also be used independently with ease. At HSK4 level, it is an elegant structure frequently encountered in both spoken and written Chinese that carries the meaning "expectation-breaking but."

tables.caption_tr: 却 (què) Position Rules in Sentences
rows: 他却不知道。 [Tā què bù zhīdào.]

我很想去，但是我却没有时间。 [Wǒ hěn xiǎng qù, dànshì wǒ què méiyǒu shíjiān.]
但是/可是 cümle başında bağlaç görevi görür; 却 ikinci cümlenin öznesinden sonra gelip vurguyu pekiştirir.
虽然他很累，他却继续工作。 [Suīrán tā hěn lèi, tā què jìxù gōngzuò.]
虽然 ile kurulan 'gerçi' cümlesinin ardından 却, beklenene ters sonucu bildirir; 但是 olmadan da kullanılabilir.
但是/可是'nin aksine 却 asla cümlenin en başında, öznenin önünde kullanılamaz.
Özne + 却 + 也/又/还 + Fiil
他却也不生气。 [Tā què yě bù shēngqì.]
却, 也/又/还 gibi başka zarflarla yan yana kullanılabilir; sırayla 却 önce gelir.

yaoshi-dehua.title_tr: Types of Conditions: 要是[yàoshi] and ...的话[dehuà]
yaoshi-dehua.intro_tr: In Chinese, conditional sentences with the meaning "if, ...then" are most commonly constructed with the conjunctions 要是[yàoshi] and 如果[rúguǒ]; in the result clause, the adverb 就[jiù] usually appears. 的话[dehuà], on the other hand, is a particle added to the END of the conditional clause, which reinforces the meaning of "...if" and is particularly common in spoken language; it can be used alone or together with 要是/如果. In these constructions corresponding to the Turkish suffix "-se/-sa", the basic rule is: first the conditional clause, then the result clause beginning with 就. 要是 is the most casual/intimate option, 如果 is neutral and common, 假如[jiǎrú]/假使[jiǎshǐ] are more formal written language options. These different markers can be used interchangeably; what is important is that the conditional-result logic is constructed in the correct order.

budan-erqie.title_tr: 不但...而且... — "Not only... but also..."
budan-erqie.intro_tr: The structure 不但...而且... [búdàn...érqiě...] connects two clauses together and conveys the meaning of the Turkish "not only ... but also ..." in English; the second clause adds to the first and typically provides stronger information. This pattern is a fundamental conjunction structure frequently encountered at the HSK4 level, used in both spoken and written language. If the subject is the same in both clauses, 不但 [búdàn] is placed after the subject; if the subject is different, it is placed before the subject (at the beginning of the sentence). In the second clause, 而且 [érqiě] is generally used together with an adverb such as 也 [yě], 还 [hái], or 更 [gèng] to reinforce the emphasis. For learners starting from zero level, the easiest learning path is to first memorize the "same subject" pattern, then move on to the "different subject" pattern.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure: Placement of 不但 [búdàn] According to Subject Position
rows: Özne + 不但[búdàn] + Yüklem1，而且[érqiě] + Yüklem2
他不但聪明，而且努力。[tā búdàn cōngmíng, érqiě nǔlì.]
O sadece zeki değil, üstelik çalışkan da.
不但[búdàn] + Özne1 + Yüklem1，而且[érqiě] + Özne2 + (也/还) + Yüklem2
不但他聪明，而且他姐姐也聪明。[búdàn tā cōngmíng, érqiě tā jiějie yě cōngmíng.]
Sadece o zeki değil, üstelik ablası da zeki.
footnotes_tr: Rule: If the subject is the same, 不但 comes AFTER the subject; if the subject is different, 不但 comes at the BEGINNING OF THE SENTENCE, before the subject.

nandao-rhetorical.title_tr: 难道 (nándào): Rhetorical Question "Isn't it... ?" or "Could it be... ?"
nandao-rhetorical.intro_tr: 难道[nándào] is a rhetorical question particle that uses the grammatical structure of a question sentence but does not actually ask a question; rather, it emphasizes the speaker's strong conviction or astonishment. It corresponds to expressions like "Isn't it... ?", "Could it be... ?" or "...isn't it?" in English, and does not expect an answer; the speaker already knows what the answer is. 难道 typically appears at the beginning of a sentence or immediately after the subject, and the sentence usually ends with 吗[ma] or a question mark. The important logical rule is this: if the sentence is negative, the real meaning is affirmative; if the sentence is affirmative, the real meaning is negative — in other words, the meaning is reversed. This structure is used in both everyday conversation and formal writing to express objection, show astonishment, or emphatically defend an opinion.

daodi-jiujing.title_tr: 到底 [dàodǐ] / 究竟 [jiūjìng] — 'For God's Sake, Actually, Really'
daodi-jiujing.intro_tr: 到底[dàodǐ] and 究竟[jiūjìng] are intensive adverbs that correspond to expressions in Turkish like "for God's sake, really, actually, what on earth." They typically appear before question words (什么, 谁, 怎么, 为什么, 哪儿) or the V-不-V structure in interrogative sentences, emphasizing curiosity, impatience, or a demand for a definite answer; they add an air of "come on, settle this already, what exactly is this" rather than just asking a straightforward question. 到底 can also be used in affirmative (positive) sentences with the meaning "in the end, ultimately"; 究竟 is used very rarely in this second sense and is more formal/characteristic of written language. Neither is used with plain 吗-questions (yes/no questions); they necessarily require a question word or V-不-V structure. For a beginner student, the most practical tip is: when you see these words, translating the sentence as "for God's sake..." or "what exactly..." usually gives the right result.

buguan-dou.title_tr: 不管[bùguǎn]...都[dōu]... (regardless of / Unconditional Result Structure)
buguan-dou.intro_tr: The 不管[bùguǎn]...都[dōu]... structure is a very common pattern used to express that, regardless of under what conditions an event occurs, the result will never change. 不管[bùguǎn] by itself means 'regardless, without regard' and is typically used either with a question word (谁[shéi], 什么[shénme], 怎么[zěnme], 哪儿[nǎr], 多少[duōshao], etc.) or with an 'A 还是[háishi] B' (whether A or B) structure. In the second clause, there must be 都[dōu] or 也[yě]; this word carries the emphasis 'in any case, nonetheless' and if omitted, the sentence is considered incomplete/incorrect. While 不管 is very frequently used in spoken language, 无论[wúlùn], which is nearly identical in meaning, is preferred in formal and written language. For a beginner student, the easiest mnemonic is as follows: '不管 + [condition/question word], 都 + [result]' = '... no matter what, [result] does not change.'

不管'dan sonra gelir; mümkün olan TÜM durumları/koşulları temsil eder (belirsizlik anlamıyla kullanılır, gerçek soru değildir).

shenzhi.intro_tr: 甚至[shènzhì] meaning "even, moreover" is an adverb/conjunction used to emphasize the most extreme, unexpected, or surprising item in a series of examples. It typically works with the logic of "progressing from what's normal to the most extreme example": "A does it, B does it, even C does it." 甚至 can appear both before and after the subject, and its meaning doesn't change, only the emphasized element changes. To further strengthen the emphasis, it's often combined with the structure 连...都/也..., creating the pattern 甚至连...都/也.... At the HSK4 level, it's frequently encountered in both spoken and written Chinese, an important word that adds a dramatic "even such a thing" tone to sentences.

separable-verbs.title_tr: Separable Verbs 离合词[líhécí] (见面, 帮忙, 睡觉)
separable-verbs.intro_tr: 离合词[líhécí], that is "separable verbs," are words that consist of a combination of a verb and an object (usually an abstract object) but behave grammatically like a single verb. For example, in 见面[jiànmiàn], there is the verb 见[jiàn] "to see" and the object 面[miàn] "face"; together they mean "to meet/to see each other." The most important characteristic of these structures is that even though they appear as a single word, grammatically other elements (了, 过, 着, duration, frequency, measure words, possessive 的) can be inserted BETWEEN them — that is, they are "sepa"rable. Furthermore, these verbs cannot directly take a person as an object after them; instead, the structure 跟/和 + person + verb is used. The most commonly encountered examples at HSK4 level are verbs like 见面, 帮忙, 睡觉, 结婚, 生气, 毕业, 请假, 聊天.

yushi-yinci.title_tr: 于是 / 因此 — 'Thereupon' and 'Therefore' Resultative Conjunctions
yushi-yinci.intro_tr: 于是[yúshì] and 因此[yīncǐ] are both conjunctions that link two sentences with a 'result' relationship, but their emphasis differs. 于是[yúshì] describes a second event that occurs as a natural continuation or reaction immediately following an event — it is similar to the Turkish expression 'thereupon, following that' and is typically used in narrative (story) sentences. 因此[yīncǐ], on the other hand, establishes a more logical causal relationship, meaning 'for this reason, therefore', and compared to 所以[suǒyǐ], it has a more formal tone and is closer to written language. Both are typically positioned between two sentences, at the beginning of the second sentence, and there must always be a sentence before them that indicates a cause or event. This structure is a fundamental discourse device frequently encountered at HSK4 level, making written expression fluent and connected.

yi-jiu.intro_tr: The 一...就... structure expresses a very short time interval between two events and corresponds to the Turkish '-er -ermez' pattern. At the moment the first verb (the action marked with 一) occurs, the second verb (the action marked with 就) happens immediately afterwards. This structure can be used to describe both one-time events and automatic reactions that have become habitual ("whenever ... then ..."). The subject is placed in different positions depending on whether there is one or two subjects in the sentence. Additionally, the tone of the 一 character changes according to the tone of the syllable that follows it; attention should be paid to this rule.

jinguan-danshi.intro_tr: The 尽管[jǐnguǎn]...但是[dànshì]... structure corresponds to the Turkish pattern "even though... still..." or "admittedly... but..." and connects a realized, definite situation to the consequence that emerges despite that situation. In the first sentence, 尽管[jǐnguǎn] presents a fact that is unexpected or seems negative; in the second sentence, 但是[dànshì] (or 可是[kěshì], 却[què], 还是[háishi]) indicates the result that occurs despite that fact. This structure is semantically almost identical to 虽然[suīrán]...但是[dànshì]...; the difference is that 尽管[jǐnguǎn] carries a somewhat stronger emphasis and a tone of "acceptance" or "resignation" and is used only for actual/definite events (not for hypothetical situations). The subject can come before or after 尽管[jǐnguǎn]; if the two sentences have different subjects, the subject must absolutely come after 尽管[jǐnguǎn].

haoxiang-sihu.title_tr: 好像 [hǎoxiàng] / 似乎 [sìhū] — 'Like, seem to appear' or 'It seems like...'
haoxiang-sihu.intro_tr: 好像[hǎoxiàng] and 似乎[sìhū] are adverbs that correspond to Turkish expressions 'sanki', 'gibi görünüyor', 'galiba'; they are used when making uncertain observations, guesses, or comparisons. Both come after the subject and before the predicate in a sentence, and they show that the speaker is not 100% certain, but rather making a judgment based on an impression or indicator. 好像 is a flexible word that is used very frequently both in everyday speech and in writing; 似乎, on the other hand, has a more formal and literary tone, and is generally preferred in written language and serious conversations. 好像 can also be used together with 一样[yíyàng] or 似的[shìde] to construct a direct comparison sentence in the form of 'sanki...-mış gibi'; 似乎 is almost never used in this way. Since both words are adverbs, not verbs, they are not used directly with a noun, but always together with a clause or predicate.

qianwan-imperative.title_tr: 千万[qiānwàn]: "Don't, Under Any Circumstances" — Warning Adverb
qianwan-imperative.intro_tr: Although 千万[qiānwàn] originally refers to the number "ten million", its most frequently encountered usage in grammar is as an ADVERB meaning "don't", "under any circumstances", "absolutely". This adverbial usage appears ONLY in imperative/warning sentences — it is never used in plain statements or interrogative sentences. It typically combines with 别[bié] or 不要[búyào] to form a strong prohibition ("千万别...", "千万不要..."); in positive commands, it appears with 要[yào] ("千万要..."). It emphasizes the speaker's serious concern and insistence, so it is very similar to the Turkish expression "don't, I'm telling you!"

footnotes_tr: 千万 generally appears at the beginning of the sentence (before the subject) or immediately after the subject: 千万你别去 / 你千万别去 (both are natural).

shouxian-qici.title_tr: Discourse Markers: 首先 / 其次 / 最后
shouxian-qici.intro_tr: Discourse markers (话语顺序词[huàyǔ shùnxùcí]) are conjunctive words used to present ideas, steps, or reasons in order in speech or writing. 首先[shǒuxiān] ("first, firstly"), 其次[qícì] ("second, then") and 最后[zuìhòu] ("finally, lastly") form the most common triplet and are often used together to organize a list or process. These words are used at the beginning of a sentence, separated by commas, and generally come before the subject. While the pattern 先[xiān]...然后[ránhòu]...最后[zuìhòu] is more frequently heard in spoken language, the pattern 首先...其次...最后 is preferred in more formal presentations, articles, and discussions. This structure can express both temporal order (the steps you take) and logical sequence (the arguments you propose).

buru-comparison.title_tr: 不如 / 没有...那么 (Negative Comparison)
buru-comparison.intro_tr: The structures 不如[bùrú] and 没有[méiyǒu]...那么[nàme] are used in Chinese to compare two things and express that one is not "as" as the other; they correspond to the Turkish phrase "...not as, ...less than." The structure 没有...那么/这么[zhème] is used with an adjective to neutrally indicate that A is not as (adjective) as B. 不如[bùrú], on the other hand, carries a stronger, evaluative meaning; it conveys the idea that "A is worse/more inadequate than B" or "it would be better to do/prefer B" and can be used without an adjective. Both patterns can be thought of as a kind of negative counterpart to the positive comparison built with 比[bǐ] (A 比 B + adjective); however, they are never used together with 比. On this page, the structure of both patterns, the nuances between them, and common mistakes are summarized in table form.

lian-dou.intro_tr: The 连...都/也 [lián...dōu/yě] pattern is the exact equivalent of the phrase "... even" in English and is used to emphasize how extreme, unexpected, or unusual a situation is. The structure marks the most salient element in the sentence (which can be the subject, object, verb, number, or time expression) with 连 [lián], then reinforces this emphasis with 都 [dōu] or 也 [yě]. It is generally found in negative or surprising sentences describing that even the "smallest, easiest, most likely" thing did not happen or did happen. 都 and 也 are nearly identical in meaning and can be freely substituted for each other; the choice is mostly a matter of style. This pattern is extremely common in both spoken and written language and is one of the basic emphasis structures at HSK4 level.

ba-construction-full.title_tr: 把 (bǎ) Structure Complete Scope — Complement Obligation
ba-construction-full.intro_tr: The most critical rule of 把 (bǎ) structure is this: in a 把 sentence, the verb can NEVER be bare (naked) — after the verb there must always be a complement, 了, reduplication, or some other element, otherwise the sentence is grammatically incorrect. This rule answers the question 'Why does 把 require a mandatory complement': the 把 structure describes that a specific object REACHES a definite result/state/location, which is why the 'result' must necessarily be expressed in the language. This page comprehensively lists ALL types of complements that can follow the verb (result, direction, duration-frequency, 了, reduplication, 一下, 在/到/给/成) and the correct position of negation. Purpose: to identify and correct incorrect sentences that are left bare in the form '把 + object + verb'.

xiaqu-continue.title_tr: 下去 (xiàqu): Continuing an Action (说下去)
xiaqu-continue.intro_tr: 下去[xiàqu] is actually a directional complement that means 'to go down', but when used after a verb, it usually acquires a figurative meaning and means 'to continue an ongoing action, to proceed'. The structure is simple: Verb + 下去, for example 说下去[shuōxiaqu] 'to continue explaining'. This pattern generally expresses the speaker continuing an action they have begun or telling someone to 'continue'; therefore it frequently appears in polite request sentences like 请继续...下去[qǐng jìxù...xiàqu]. For negation, 不 or 得 is inserted between the verb and 下去 (说不下去 'cannot continue', 说得下去 'can continue'), and for an imperative that wants to end the action, the pattern 别/不要...下去了 is used. The concrete/directional usage of 下去 (for example 'to go down, to put down') must be distinguished from its figurative/continuity usage (continuing an action) based on context.

kongpa.title_tr: 恐怕 (kǒngpà): "I'm afraid that" — Negative Prediction Adverb
kongpa.intro_tr: 恐怕[kǒngpà] is an adverb that corresponds to the Turkish expressions "I'm afraid that", "I suspect (unfortunately)" and expresses the speaker's PERSONAL PREDICTION about a negative, unpleasant, or worrying situation. The difference from neutral probability adverbs like 也许[yěxǔ] or 可能[kěnéng] is that 恐怕[kǒngpà] almost always points to a bad, unwanted, or sad outcome — like the weather will be bad, someone won't come, there won't be enough time. In a sentence, it generally appears right after the subject, sometimes at the beginning of the sentence, and is usually used together with elements like 了[le], 不[bù], 没有[méiyǒu]. At HSK4 level, it frequently appears both in everyday speech to express a polite objection and in written narratives to express predictions. On this page, we summarize 恐怕[kǒngpà]'s position, its difference from similar words, and common mistakes in tables.

potential-complements.title_tr: Capability Complements (V得/不 + Complement): 听得懂 / 听不懂
potential-complements.intro_tr: Capability complements (可能补语[kěnéng bǔyǔ]), a special structure that expresses whether an action can or cannot be "performed" physically or mentally; it corresponds to the Turkish meaning of "-ebilmek / -ememek" but is embedded within result or directional complements. The structure is formed by inserting 得[de] (positive: "can do") or 不[bù] (negative: "cannot do") in the middle of the patterns you already know, such as "Result Complements" (听懂, 看完, etc.) or "Directional Complements" (回来, 进去, etc.). For example, the verb 听懂[tīngdǒng] "to hear and understand" transforms into 听得懂[tīng de dǒng] "to be able to hear and understand" and 听不懂[tīng bu dǒng] "to be unable to hear and understand". This structure is especially frequently used when describing "inability to do something due to obstacles/insufficiency" and is much more natural in spoken language than the 能[néng]+verb+complement structure. The most important point for students starting from zero level: 得/不 always goes between the verb and the complement, never inserted anywhere else.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure: Affirmative, Negative, and Question Form
rows: 听得懂吗[tīng de dǒng ma]?
听得懂听不懂[tīng de dǒng tīng bu dǒng]?
footnotes_tr: 得[de] is written the same as '的/地/得' here but is a different grammatical particle: placed before the result/directional complement, it adds the meaning of 'capability'.
In the question form, it is generally sufficient to end with 吗; the V不V repetition pattern feels somewhat more formal/emphatic.

tables.caption_tr: Common Capability Patterns with Result Complements
footnotes_tr: *买起 is not used alone; 买得起/买不起 is a fixed expression that exists only as a capability pattern (carries the meaning of material affordability).

tables.caption_tr: Common Capability Patterns with Directional Complements
footnotes_tr: In compound directional complements (起来, 下去, 出来), 得/不 is inserted right in the middle of the two-syllable complement, before the first syllable (来/去/上/下): 做得出来, 做不出来.

太晚了,来不及了。(Çok geç, artık yetişmez.)
他对得起父母。(Ailesine karşı yüzü ak.)

这样做说不过去。(Böyle yapmak izah edilemez.)
arada çok fark var (olumsuzda kullanılır: 差不多)
他俩水平差得多。(İkisinin seviyesi çok farklı.)
这两个差不多一样。(Bu ikisi neredeyse aynı.)
footnotes_tr: These patterns have now become idioms on their own; they are used even more frequently in daily conversation than the result complement patterns.

gang-vs-gangcai.title_tr: 刚 (gāng) vs 刚才 (gāngcái): The Difference of 'Recently'
gang-vs-gangcai.intro_tr: Both 刚[gāng] and 刚才[gāngcái] are translated into Turkish as "demin, a moment ago," which is why beginning-level students often confuse them. The fundamental difference between them lies in their grammatical (syntactic) category: 刚 is an ADVERB (副词), always standing directly before the verb and cannot be used alone in a sentence; 刚才, on the other hand, is a TEMPORAL NOUN (时间名词), which can appear at the beginning of a sentence, before/after the subject, serve as a standalone answer, and form possessive constructions with 的. While 刚 only emphasizes that "the action occurred in the recent past," 刚才 refers to "a specific time period just before the present moment," and other things may have happened during that time period as well. The two can sometimes be used together in the same sentence (刚才刚) and this strengthens the meaning of "truly just now."

budebu.title_tr: 不得不 (bùdébù): 'Must/Be Forced To' - Involuntary Obligation
budebu.intro_tr: The 不得不[bùdébù] expression is a very useful pattern that describes a person being forced to perform an action due to external circumstances, beyond their own will. The structure actually consists of a double negation: 不[bù] + 得[dé] (to be able to/to be possible) + 不[bù], which literally means 'it is not possible to not do it'; this semantically transforms into 'being forced to do it'. In the sentence it always appears immediately after the subject and before the main verb, and typically a reason (因为, 由于) or situation is stated first. This pattern emphasizes obligation arising from a helpless situation rather than from a mere grammar rule or personal duty, and carries a tone of slight reluctance/regret. The most important point for a beginner student is not to confuse this structure with 应该[yīnggāi] (suggestion) or 必须[bìxū] (neutral obligation).

tables.caption_tr: 不得不 Basic Sentence Structure
rows: 因为/由于 + Sebep，Özne + 不得不 + Fiil
因为下雨，我们不得不取消比赛。[Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, wǒmen bùdébù qǔxiāo bǐsài.]
Yağmur yüzünden maçı iptal etmek zorunda kaldık.
Özne + 不得不 + Fiil + 了
他不得不放弃了。[Tā bùdébù fàngqì le.]
我们不得不接受这个结果。[Wǒmen bùdébù jiēshòu zhège jiéguǒ.]
Bu sonucu kabul etmek zorunda kaldık.
footnotes_tr: 不得不 always comes after the subject and before the verb; the verb itself remains affirmative, only the 不's inside the pattern are negated.

tables.caption_tr: 不得不 and Comparison of Similar Obligation Expressions
rows: Dış koşulun zorlamasıyla oluşan çaresizlik; 'yapmamak elde değil'
我不得不同意。[Wǒ bùdébù tóngyì.] - Kabul etmek zorunda kaldım.
Başka seçenek kalmadığı için 'sadece bu yapılabilir'; sonuç/çözümsüzlük vurgusu
没有车，我只好走路。[Méiyǒu chē, wǒ zhǐhǎo zǒulù.] - Araç olmadığı için yürümek zorunda kaldım.
Nötr, kural veya görev gereği kesin zorunluluk; duygu içermez
你必须完成作业。[Nǐ bìxū wánchéng zuòyè.] - Ödevini tamamlaman gerekiyor.
不得不'ye çok yakın anlam, biraz daha yazı diline özgü çifte olumsuzlama
我不能不承认。[Wǒ bùnéng bù chéngrèn.] - Kabul etmemem mümkün değil.
Ahlaki/mantıksal öneri, tavsiye; kesin zorunluluk değildir
你应该多休息。[Nǐ yīnggāi duō xiūxi.] - Daha çok dinlenmelisin.
footnotes_tr: 不得不 and 只好 can often be used interchangeably, but 不得不 carries a stronger feeling of 'being crushed under obligation'.

tables.caption_tr: 不得不 and Commonly Seen Verb Patterns
footnotes_tr: Patterns like 不得不说 and 不得不佩服 are also used in spoken language as an independent discourse marker, giving the feeling of 'I must admit that'.

tables.caption_tr: 不得不 Usage with Cause/Purpose Conjunctions
rows: 由于 + Sebep，Özne + 不得不 + Fiil
由于时间不够，我们不得不提前结束。[Yóuyú shíjiān búgòu, wǒmen bùdébù tíqián jiéshù.]
Zaman yetmediğinden erken bitirmek zorunda kaldık.
为了 + Amaç，Özne + 不得不 + Fiil
为了健康，他不得不戒烟。[Wèile jiànkāng, tā bùdébù jièyān.]
Sağlığı için sigarayı bırakmak zorunda kaldı.
因为 + Sebep，Özne + 不得不 + Fiil
因为下大雨，我们不得不留在家里。[Yīnwèi xià dàyǔ, wǒmen bùdébù liú zài jiālǐ.]
Şiddetli yağmur yüzünden evde kalmak zorunda kaldık.
footnotes_tr: The 不得不 pattern almost always comes as a response to a reason or negative situation stated in the previous sentence; use without a reason is not natural.
